thread:
ana: Heads up — hosted-prod p99 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.6s around 14:02 UTC, p95 also elevated. Dash: https://dash.redwood/prod/latency (screenshot attached). Anyone seeing related alerts?

infra-bot: Incident alert: hosted-api.p99 latency spike > 1s for 5m, affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Rate limit backlog rising.

kevin: Noticed the kernel-selector tweak rolled at 2026-03-17T23:40 by @luke (commit 9a7b3c4). That changed affinity thresholds for aux kernels. Could be misselect under certain seq distributions.

maria: Pushed a quick profile from a handful of p99 traces (attached). Flame summary: heavy time in `fallback_copy_kv` and `aux_kernel_dispatch` with frequent `kernel_fallback` events. Snippet: 
```
# perf summary (top stacks)
fallback_copy_kv  42%  aux_kernel_dispatch  33%  token_emit 15%
# kernel_fallback: 1200 events in 5m
```

sasha: kvcache metrics show a hotshard and eviction spike starting ~14:00. `kvcache.evictions_per_min 385 -> 3200`, `kvcache.hit_rate 0.87 -> 0.52`. Looks like a tenant is priming long prefixes.

jon: Queue depth histogram from the runtime at 14:04: 
```
queue_depth: 0: 68%, 1-5: 20%, 6-20: 8%, 21-50: 3%, >50: 1%
avg_wait_ms: 140 -> 680 (tail)
```

kevin: That aligns — when kvcache misses spike, requests block waiting on KV priming which pushes more into aux kernels and forces fallback paths (slower kernels). The selector threshold change might have made us prefer aux kernels earlier, which exacerbates priming for some workloads.

luke: I can revert the selector commit to previous thresholds as a canary on 3 hosts. Rolling revert now to canary pool `hosted-canary-3`. `deploy-bot`: rolling revert queued.

deploy-bot: deploy started: revert 9a7b3c4 -> 4f2d1a0 to hosted-canary-3 (3 hosts). ETA ~2m.

ana: (typo) — ana: ack. Also temporarily bumping kvcache size on canary to reduce evictions: `kvcache.max_entries += 25%` on those hosts.

maria: small profiling after canary revert (approx 2m post-revert): `kernel_fallback` events dropped from 1200/5m to ~90/5m on canary, kvcache.evictions_per_min down to ~420, hit_rate back to 0.81.

jon: rate limiter backlog cleared on canary, avg_wait_ms down to 180ms, p99 ~240ms.

kevin: Good signal. We'll keep canary for 10m then roll revert to 25% if stable. Parallel action: add short-term per-tenant priming cap to limit long-prefix priming (throttle priming tasks per-tenant to 4 concurrent). Sasha, can you open a follow-up PR for the priming cap?

sasha: on it, will draft PR and add e2e. Also logging patch to emit tenant id for high priming tasks for postmortem.

luke: rolling revert to 25% (hosted-pool-1) now. Deploy log: `revert 4f2d1a0 -> applied to 18 hosts`

deploy-bot: deploy success.

ana: prod-wide metrics 6m after first canary revert: p99 back to 260ms, p95 120ms. No further alerts.

kevin: Root cause (working hypothesis): kernel-selector sensitivity change caused earlier aux kernel selection under long-prefix workloads -> increased KV priming -> hotshard evictions -> queue depth/backpressure -> fallback kernels and latency tail. Mitigations: revert selector change, temporary kvcache increase, priming concurrency cap, and better observability (tenant id in priming logs).

maria: action items assigned in incident board: revert already, PR for priming cap (#4521), observability patch (#4522), longer-term: refine kernel selector model with seq-length distribution features.

ana: thumbs up. I'll kick off a short postmortem doc and include flame samples. Please add any traces you captured to the doc. :thumbsup:

kevin: adding note — consider adding a canary traffic profile that includes long-prefix synthetic traces to catch this before rollout.

jon: confirmed resolved — closing incident in 30m if no regressions.

ana: thanks everyone. Great cross-team triage. :party_parrot:
